title: Fuselage — Fwd Lower Shell Lap Joints — Re-Sealing and Splice Plate Renewal
abstract: In-service re-sealing of the forward lower shell longitudinal lap joints with renewal of the aft splice plate, restoring the corrosion protection on aircraft that show filiform corrosion under the fastener heads.

sections.planning_reason: Filiform and exfoliation corrosion has been reported on the forward lower shell longitudinal lap joints of early classic aircraft, concentrated where the cargo compartment floor drains discharge onto the lower shell. Twenty-nine findings were recorded across the affected population between 2013 and 2016 and four had already reached the allowable damage limit, which turns a blend-out into an engineering repair with its own inspection programme. Aircraft that are not brought to the improved sealing standard will continue to accumulate findings and will eventually need a structural repair.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin opens the longitudinal lap joint locally between stations 1080 and 1360 on both sides of the lower shell, removes the existing aft splice plate, cleans and re-treats the faying surfaces, applies a chromate-inhibited interfay sealant and re-fastens the joint wet. The lower shell clip is retained where its condition permits and renewed where corrosion has reduced the flange thickness beyond the blend limit.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Get access to the forward and aft cargo compartments and remove the floor panels and the lower lining between stations 1080 and 1360. Do a detailed visual inspection of the joint and record every corrosion finding with its position relative to the nearest frame. Remove the fasteners along the joint and remove the splice plate ORV288354-46. Clean the faying surfaces and blend out corrosion inside the allowable limits. Do an eddy current inspection of every fastener hole and report any indication before you continue. Apply the surface treatment of ATA 51-20 to all bare surfaces. Apply the interfay sealant bead along the full joint length. Install the renewed splice plate and the clip D5321122023477 and re-fasten wet with rivets AES645587-2A to the pattern of drawing D53211223480. Do a leak check of the cargo compartment drain path. Install the lining and the floor panels and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to ZEPHYR-20 and ZEPHYR-22 aircraft in the MSN range Z00051 to Z01993. The range was drawn from the delivery records of the aircraft that carry the original interfay sealing standard on the forward lower shell lap joints.
sections.material_note: Kit K5321-1004-01 contains the splice plate, the clip, the fastener set and the consumables for one aircraft. Lead time is fourteen weeks from order. The removed splice plate is not returned and may be scrapped locally once the embodiment is recorded.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled structural check, or within 60 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

title: Fuselage — Fwd Lower Shell Lap Joints — Re-Sealing and Splice Plate Renewal

issue.reason: The effectivity is re-stated in terms of the external bonded strap standard, with the MSN range kept for guidance only.

abstract: In-service re-sealing of the forward lower shell longitudinal lap joints with renewal of the aft splice plate, now effective on configuration rather than on serial number: any aircraft whose joint is not yet at the bonded strap standard.

sections.planning_reason: Filiform and exfoliation corrosion has been reported on the forward lower shell longitudinal lap joints of early classic aircraft, concentrated where the cargo compartment floor drains discharge onto the lower shell. Twenty-nine findings were recorded across the affected population between 2013 and 2016 and four had already reached the allowable damage limit, which turns a blend-out into an engineering repair with its own inspection programme. Aircraft that are not brought to the improved sealing standard will continue to accumulate findings and will eventually need a structural repair.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin opens the longitudinal lap joint locally between stations 1080 and 1360 on both sides of the lower shell, removes the existing aft splice plate, cleans and re-treats the faying surfaces, applies a chromate-inhibited interfay sealant and re-fastens the joint wet. The lower shell clip is retained where its condition permits and renewed where corrosion has reduced the flange thickness beyond the blend limit.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Get access to the forward and aft cargo compartments and remove the floor panels and the lower lining between stations 1080 and 1360. Do a detailed visual inspection of the joint and record every corrosion finding with its position relative to the nearest frame. Remove the fasteners along the joint and remove the splice plate ORV288354-46. Clean the faying surfaces and blend out corrosion inside the allowable limits. Do an eddy current inspection of every fastener hole and report any indication before you continue. Apply the surface treatment of ATA 51-20 to all bare surfaces. Install the lining and the floor panels and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Effectivity is stated on configuration. This bulletin applies to ZEPHYR-20 and ZEPHYR-22 aircraft whose forward lower shell longitudinal lap joints have not been brought to the external bonded strap standard of MOD-153870, whatever their manufacturer serial number. The MSN range Z00051 to Z01993 is retained as guidance only, because the strap population has since been widened and the range no longer describes the same set of aircraft. Aircraft already carrying the bonded strap must not be re-worked to this bulletin: the strap covers the joint that this bulletin opens. Confirm the joint standard from the aircraft configuration record before you order the kit.
sections.material_note: Kit K5321-1004-01 contains the splice plate, the clip, the fastener set and the consumables for one aircraft. Lead time is fourteen weeks from order. Do not order the kit until the joint standard has been confirmed, because a kit ordered for an aircraft that has since been strapped is not returnable. The removed splice plate is not returned and may be scrapped locally once the embodiment is recorded.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled structural check, or within 60 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.

revision_history.reason: Effectivity re-stated against the bonded strap standard; MSN range retained for guidance only and a configuration check added before kit order
